results.content:

 Enterprise: PayPal runs 74,000 Perplexity queries a week across 3,700+ weekly users (2026)
 Cloud: a three-year US$750m Microsoft Azure agreement signed in January 2026

## Enterprise adoption and IPO [...] Amazon Web Services: Perplexity's preferred cloud provider. It was one of the first customers on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, which it uses to train and serve models, and worked with the Amazon Bedrock team on security, scale and privacy.

The trigger was Computer, a cloud agent launched in February that orchestrates 19 AI models to research, write and code on a user's behalf.

Revenue reportedly jumped 50% in the month after launch, and NVIDIA is said to be weighing a new round that would value the AI search challenger at more than US$30bn.

message.content:
## Recent developments
* **Teammates Launch & Expansion:** Perplexity deployed its proactive agentic AI feature, "Teammates" (initially for Perplexity Max subscribers), expanding availability from iOS and web to the Mac app [4, 6]. The feature allows AI agents to handle ongoing tasks like QA, customer service, and research independently [4, 6].
* **Open-Weights Model Release:** On November 13, 2026, Perplexity released open weights for `pplx-decider-v1.3` and `pplx-decider-flash-v1.3` under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face, built on fine-tuned Qwen architectures for text-span extraction and routing [1].
* **Financial & Scale Growth:** Perplexity's AI answer engine hit a US$750m run-rate, fueled by enterprise adoption (such as PayPal running 74,000 queries weekly) and a 3-year US$750m Microsoft Azure agreement [2]. 
* **Legal Challenges:** A class-action lawsuit was filed against Perplexity AI in a California federal court by plaintiff Ntsikelelo Bonga, alleging the company misleads consumers regarding undisclosed usage caps on paid subscription features [3].

## Talking points
* **Agentic Ecosystem (`Computer` & `Teammates`):** Discuss how the shift toward long-running agents that persist after closing tabs [9]—and can run fully locally on Mac hardware [7]—changes the value proposition from a search answer box to full workflow automation [6].
* **Enterprise Expansion:** Review the rapid enterprise scaling (e.g., PayPal integration [2]) and how the Microsoft Azure partnership [2] supports infrastructure demands.
* **Open-Source Strategy:** Evaluate the strategic impact of open-sourcing the `pplx-decider-v1.3` weights on Hugging Face [1] for developer ecosystems and research workflows.
* **Legal and Compliance Risks:** Address the recent class-action lawsuit concerning paid tier usage limits [3] and how transparent communication around subscription caps can be improved.

## Open questions
* How will Perplexity address the California class-action lawsuit regarding usage caps on paid tiers, and will this prompt changes to subscription transparency?
* What are the monetization and infrastructure cost implications of scaling local Mac execution alongside cloud-orchestrated "Teammates"?
* How does the adoption rate of the new `pplx-decider-v1.3` open weights compare to competing routing and text-classification models?

## Sources
* [Perplexity Decider v1.3 & Flash Open Weights — CASRAI](https://casrai.org/news/perplexity-pplx-decider-v1-3-open-weights-release-2026)

## Recent developments
* **Teammates Launch & Expansion:** Perplexity deployed its proactive agentic AI feature, "Teammates" (initially for Perplexity Max subscribers), expanding availability from iOS and web to the Mac app [4, 6]. The feature allows AI agents to handle ongoing tasks like QA, customer service, and research independently [4, 6].
* **Open-Weights Model Release:** On November 13, 2026, Perplexity released open weights for `pplx-decider-v1.3` and `pplx-decider-flash-v1.3` under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face, built on fine-tuned Qwen architectures for text-span extraction and routing [1].
* **Financial & Scale Growth:** Perplexity's AI answer engine hit a US$750m run-rate, fueled by enterprise adoption (such as PayPal running 74,000 queries weekly) and a 3-year US$750m Microsoft Azure agreement [2]. 
* **Legal Challenges:** A class-action lawsuit was filed against Perplexity AI in a California federal court by plaintiff Ntsikelelo Bonga, alleging the company misleads consumers regarding undisclosed usage caps on paid subscription features [3].

## Talking points
* **Agentic Ecosystem (`Computer` & `Teammates`):** Discuss how the shift toward long-running agents that persist after closing tabs [9]—and can run fully locally on Mac hardware [7]—changes the value proposition from a search answer box to full workflow automation [6].
* **Enterprise Expansion:** Review the rapid enterprise scaling (e.g., PayPal integration [2]) and how the Microsoft Azure partnership [2] supports infrastructure demands.
* **Open-Source Strategy:** Evaluate the strategic impact of open-sourcing the `pplx-decider-v1.3` weights on Hugging Face [1] for developer ecosystems and research workflows.
* **Legal and Compliance Risks:** Address the recent class-action lawsuit concerning paid tier usage limits [3] and how transparent communication around subscription caps can be improved.

## Open questions
* How will Perplexity address the California class-action lawsuit regarding usage caps on paid tiers, and will this prompt changes to subscription transparency?
* What are the monetization and infrastructure cost implications of scaling local Mac execution alongside cloud-orchestrated "Teammates"?
* How does the adoption rate of the new `pplx-decider-v1.3` open weights compare to competing routing and text-classification models?
